Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can deliver the mapping and the regression plan by COB Friday. High-level response below and attached is a short package to get started.

Attachments: redwood_governance_summary_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.8MB); nistrm_mapping.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)

Summary items:
- NIST/EU mapping: We provide a control-to-obligation matrix (attached) that maps our operational controls and platform capabilities to NIST subfunctions and EU AI Act obligations. The matrix includes control owners and references to supporting artifacts.
- Eval/regression approach: We run continuous regression suites (nightly smoke + weekly full) and targeted per-release regressions. Sampling is workload-aware: we maintain stratified prompt sets by vertical (e.g., clinical triage, administrative responses), severity, and token-length buckets. For high-risk labels (clinical diagnostic assistance), we perform denser sampling (10-15% of production queries per week) and manual review of flagged regressions.
- Metrics & thresholds: We track quality (BLEU/ROUGE when applicable), hallucination rate (false fact ratio measured against gold), safety trigger rate, and latency P95. Regression alerts are triaged against configurable thresholds; failures can block rollouts and trigger automatic rollback to a pinned model variant.
- Evidence & artifacts: Our typical diligence bundle includes SOC2 scope and timeline (SOC2 Type II available in Q1 2027 for dedicated environments), architecture diagrams, sample audit logs, KMS integration notes, and a traceability sample. Some artifacts are redacted for customer data privacy; we can provide anonymized samples.

Do you want the full XLSX mapping populated with Helix-specific column entries (owner, acceptance criteria) or a generic mapping first? If you confirm, Karthik (cc'ed) will prepare the Helix-tailored columns.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Sarah — attached is the Helix-specific deliverable and a short operational note answering your two clarifications. We also included a proposed schedule to meet your COB Friday request.

Attachments: eval-regression-proposal.docx (DOCX, 95KB)

Operational clarifications (excerpt):
- Gold label management: We maintain versioned evaluation datasets in a secure repository with role-based access controls (RBAC) and audit logging. Gold labels for clinically sensitive sets are created by our partnered clinical reviewers under NDA; labels are snapshot-versioned with immutable hashes and linked to model-eval runs in our eval database. We retain metadata (label author, timestamp, dataset version, hashing) for traceability.

- Rollback behaviors and SLA: Rollbacks are automated at the routing layer and typically complete within 60–180 seconds for a single region depending on in-flight KV cache size. For stateful sessions that rely on large KV caches, we offer two rollback modes: graceful fallback (continue serving using best-effort cache rehydration) and immediate strict rollback (switch to pinned variant and invalidate session caches). We document recommended session strategies for each mode; recommended default for Helix clinical workflows is graceful fallback to avoid abrupt session loss.

Proposed delivery schedule:
- Fri 2026-11-27 EOD: Delivered XLSX mapping populated with Helix columns, eval/regression proposal (attached), and an anonymized 30-day traceability sample (Drive link).
- Mon 2026-11-30: 60-minute technical Q&A with our engineering and compliance leads (Karthik + Marissa).

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3RedwoodGovernanceFolder (traceability sample, anonymized)
